knowledge_point.title: Constructing and Solving a Dilution Model

question.:question/problem:
A juice-processing tank initially holds $600\,\text{L}$ of liquid containing $11\,\text{kg}$ of dissolved sugar.
A solution containing $0.05\,\text{kg/L}$ of dissolved sugar is pumped into the tank at a rate of $12\,\text{L/min},$ while the completely mixed liquid is drained out at a rate of $18\,\text{L/min}.$ If the amount of sugar $Q(t),$ in kilograms, in the tank $t$ minutes after pumping begins is given by

$$
Q(t)=\alpha \,(1-\frac{t}{100})+\beta {(1-\frac{t}{100})}^{3}
$$

where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are constants, what is the value of $\alpha -\beta ?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $Q$ be the amount of dissolved substance in the tank at time $t,$ in minutes. The amount entering minus the amount leaving gives
$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}.
$$
The units of these rates are $\text{kg/min}.$

**Step 1**: Calculating the rate at which substance enters the tank.
$$
\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{in}}&=(0.05\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\cdot(12\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\\
&=(0.05\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\cdot(12\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\\&=0.6\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which substance exits the tank.
The volume is
$$
V(t)=600+12t-18t=(600-6t)\,\text{L}.
$$
The concentration is $\frac{Q}{600-6t}\,\text{kg/L}.$ Hence,
$$
\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{out}}&=(18\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{600-6t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\\
&=(18\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{600-6t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\\
&=\frac{18Q}{600-6t}\,\text{kg/min}=\frac{3Q}{100-t}\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.
$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt}&=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}\\&=0.6-\frac{3Q}{100-t}.\end{aligned}
$$
Thus,
$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{3}{100-t}Q=0.6.
$$

**Step 4**: Integrate the equation.
This is a first-order linear equation with variable coefficients. So we find the general solution using an integrating factor:
$$
\begin{aligned}I(t)&=e^{\int 3/(100-t)\,dt}\\&=e^{-3\ln|100-t|}\\&=e^{\ln (100-t)^{-3}}\\&=(100-t)^{-3}.\end{aligned}
$$
Multiplying both sides by $I(t)=(100-t)^{-3}$ yields
$$
\begin{aligned}(100-t)^{-3}\cdot(\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{3}{100-t}Q)&=(100-t)^{-3}\cdot 0.6\\
(100-t)^{-3}\frac{dQ}{dt}+3(100-t)^{-4}Q&=0.6(100-t)^{-3}\\\frac{d}{dt}(Q(100-t)^{-3})&=0.6(100-t)^{-3}.\end{aligned}
$$
Now, we integrate with respect to $t:$
$$
\begin{aligned}\int\frac{d}{dt}(Q(100-t)^{-3})\,dt&=\int 0.6(100-t)^{-3}\,dt\\Q(100-t)^{-3}&=0.6\cdot\frac{1}{2}(100-t)^{-2}+C\\Q(t)&=0.3(100-t)+C(100-t)^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
Note that $C$ is a constant of integration.
The initial condition is $Q(0)=11.$ Thus,
$$
\begin{aligned}0.3(100-0)+C(100-0)^{3}&=11\\
30+C(100)^{3}&=11\\C(100)^{3}&=-19\\C&=- \frac{19}{1000000}.\end{aligned}
$$
Finally, we obtain the following expression for $Q(t):$
$$
Q(t)=- \frac{3 t}{10} - \frac{19 \left(100 - t\right)^{3}}{1000000} + 30.
$$
Writing this in the supplied normalized form gives
$$
Q(t)=30(1-\frac{t}{100})-19(1-\frac{t}{100})^{3}.
$$
Finally, we have $\alpha=30,\beta=-19,$ and
$$
\alpha-\beta=30-(-19)=49.
$$
